transcript.text: Our Dyson (one of the V ones, purple bits) keeps cutting out after about 5-10 seconds. Not every time - some days it does a whole room fine. It's maybe 5 years old. Already cleaned the filter and checked for blockages. Battery or something else?

With the filter cleaned, no blockages and the vacuum around five years old, the battery is the most likely cause, as they wear out with age and can cut out under load. It isn't certain yet, because a charging problem can look the same, so how it runs after a full charge will help tell them apart. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the battery or charging. Charge it fully and use it on the normal mode. Is it running for its normal time now, or still short?

Still cutting out. It's usually fine straight off the charger but gets worse once the battery's partly used, and on Max it nearly always stops within a few seconds. Is it worth spending £60+ on a new battery?

For a 5-year-old Dyson V model, a new battery is often worth it, because batteries are the part that typically wears out first while the motor and body usually keep going. It's worth spending only once you're fairly sure the battery is the cause and the rest of the vacuum is in good condition, compared with what a replacement vacuum would cost you. From what you have described, the most likely cause is a worn battery. Boost or max mode drains a cordless battery in a few minutes — that's normal. Was it on boost / max mode (and have you switched to normal), or was it already on the normal mode?
It's cutting out on normal mode too, not just Max, but on Max it nearly always stops within a few seconds. Battery isn't swollen or hot, if that matters. So do you think the battery's the problem?

It does sound likely: cutting out under heavy load like Max, getting worse as the charge drops, and being about 5 years old all fit a worn battery that can't hold its voltage. It's still worth making sure it's charging properly first, as a battery that isn't getting a full charge can behave the same way. Check the charger is in a working socket and pushed fully into the vacuum (or dock), and wipe the charging contacts clean and dry. The charging light should come on. Was the charger, socket or contacts the problem (and is it sorted), does the charging light never come on, or is the charger fine with the light on?
Charger light comes on and the plug goes in properly, so the charger seems fine. Sounds like it's the battery then? Is there anything else worth checking before I buy one?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Detach the wand and floorhead and look through each part, and check the bin inlet — a coin dropped through the wand should fall straight out. Did you find a blockage and clear it, is there one you can't shift, is a hose split, or was it all clear?
Yes, I checked all of it earlier - wand, head and inlet are all clear, no blockages and no splits. Coin check aside, nothing's stuck. So is it the battery then?

Quite possibly. A five-year-old battery that's fine straight off the charger but cuts out as it runs down, especially on Max, is a classic sign of a worn battery. A jammed brush bar can also make it cut in and out. Turn the floorhead over, clear any hair or thread from the brush bar (roller) and check it turns freely by hand. Was it jammed or tangled (and is it clear now), is it broken, or did it turn freely?

I haven't checked the brush bar specifically, I only looked at the wand, head and inlet. I'll have a look at it and see if it turns freely. It also cuts out in handheld mode with no tool on, if that helps.
From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
